doc.title: Jane Ira Bloom interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 3, 1998

title: Learning saxophone in Boston schools; records at home
summary: She picked the shiny sax in third grade; her parents' Ella Fitzgerald and Ellington records.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Your start in the public school system was in Boston is that right?
Did you have the typical experience of learning sax in the school system?

You bet, yeah. A list — every student in the third grade was asked do you want to play clarinet, saxophone, trumpet, you know, I forget what it was, violin, flute, something like that, and you had to pick.
Why did you pick — or did you pick the saxophone? Was that the first instrument?
You know that’s very important you know when you’re nine years old. It was shiny. And it was different.
Was there much exposure in your home to music?

On record, yeah. My folks had a nice record collection around the house. I remember I used to listen to my mom’s Ella Fitzgerald record collection, some Duke Ellington, songs from the American Songbook were around, you know, things like that were around the house.
The alto sax, was that your instrument at that time?
I had to go through all of it.
